prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The Green Party’s 2005 manifesto offers the real choice for real change: rebuilding a sustainable society grounded in social, economic and environmental justice. Putting people and planet first, Greens reject privatisation-by-stealth and austerity politics, restore trust in public life, and act decisively on the climate emergency, inequality and war.

Economy: Shift from short-term, resource-guzzling growth to equity and resilience. Redistribute wealth via progressive income tax bands (higher rates for top earners), reform Corporation Tax with more bands so big profits pay more, tax unearned wealth with a reformed Inheritance Tax based on the recipient, and abolish National Insurance by taxing all income fairly. Pilot a Land Value Tax to replace Council Tax and Uniform Business Rates. Replace VAT with revenue-neutral eco-taxes that price pollution and waste. Localise economies through community banks, credit unions, co‑ops and local currencies; oppose joining the euro; uphold workers’ rights and shorter hours. Measure what matters with well‑being indicators, not just GDP. Introduce a universal Citizen’s Income and a Citizen’s Pension.

Energy and climate: Adopt Contraction and Convergence, cutting UK CO2 by 20% by 2010, 50% by 2020 and 85% by 2030, supported by a full carbon trading system. Replace VAT/CCL on energy with a Carbon Tax; abolish standing charges and protect low users. Drive renewables to 40% by 2020, investing in wind, solar, wave and biogas; launch a Warmer Homes Act and Smart Energy Councils to cut demand; end nuclear expansion and shift all nuclear R&D to renewables.

Welfare, health, education: Build universal, empowering welfare. Phase in a Citizen’s Income (with specialist benefits on top) and a universal, earnings‑linked Citizen’s Pension; simplify family support and boost child benefit; reduce working hours. Tackle housing shortages via council building, self‑build co‑ops, LVT reform and energy‑efficient retrofits. Restore the NHS to comprehensive, universal care; end PPPs and GATS encroachment; abolish prescription, eye test and dental charges; expand holistic care; raise health funding to at least 9% of GNP with a hypothecated NHS Tax. In education, increase funding, expand Children’s Centres, scrap tuition fees and restore grants; abolish SATs and introduce individual learning plans.

Transport and environment: Rebalance the system toward walking, cycling and public transport; divert £30bn from roads; re‑regulate buses; bring rail and tube back to public ownership; price motoring’s true costs; invest in clean vehicle R&D. Curb aviation growth, tax emissions/fuel, ban night flights, shift short‑haul to rail. Deliver Zero Waste with a national strategy, a Zero Waste Agency, 60% recycling by 2010, eco-taxes on harmful substances, and an Environmental Protection Commission. Apply the precautionary principle; ban patents on natural resources; strengthen animal welfare (end live exports, battery eggs, fur; replace vivisection).

Food and farming: Localise and green the food chain. Pass an Organics Target Bill (30% by 2012); abolish CAP/CFP and replace with support for organics, biodiversity and coastal communities; ban GM food; toughen the supermarkets’ Code of Practice and reform OFT oversight.

Crime and democracy: Prevent crime by strengthening communities—safer design, youth facilities, rapid repairs, visible staff; treat drug use as a health issue; reject ID cards. Expand community policing; enact strong gun controls; embed restorative justice; combat hate crime and violence against women; advance disability rights. Renew democracy with empowered local councils, LVT-based local taxation, citizen-initiated referenda/recall, PR for all elections, democratic regional government, an elected Lords, a written constitution, disestablishment and curtailed monarchical powers; oppose the proposed EU constitution.

Peace and global justice: Pursue a truly ethical foreign policy—withdraw from Iraq in favour of UN peacekeepers, cut military spending to the EU average, decommission nuclear weapons, and back a binding Arms Trade Treaty. Raise aid to 1% of GNI, cancel debts for the 52 poorest countries, and back a Tobin tax. Democratise global institutions (UNSC without permanent vetoes; reform IMF/World Bank). Replace or transform WTO rules with a General Agreement on Sustainable Trade (GAST) to enable fair, localised, sustainable trade. Defend asylum rights, allow work and benefits, improve decisions and appeals, and ratify UN migrant conventions—while tackling the root causes of displacement.
